title: an-idea-past-idea-is-not-an-open-idea-in-the-inbox
owner: operator_inbox is a tool with users (Law 6): the codemother dashboard consumes read_ideas/read_intentions; codemother owns the care of the code (ruling 2026-09-06). CC (Fable) builds under Akien's ruling 2026-09-07.
intention: An artifact that has moved to the next stage stops being reported at the earlier one: an idea with an intent firing or a ticket citing it is not an open idea, an intention with a ticket is not an open intention, and the operator inbox lists only what needs Akien's hand.
why: Akien 2026-09-07, verbatim: 'OK, once an idea moves past idea i should no longer see it as an idea in the operator inbox. right now i see 65 ideas as open and i think we've done at least some of them.' then 'once an idea has moved to intention it's no long open as an idea. once it's a ticket we don't disply it as an intention anymore either. for the operator inbox, it's about things i need to take action on. and if we really have 65 ideas we need to advance, then why were they not progressed with the others?' The lived symptom: every session the inbox tells him 66 ideas need his hand when 5 do, and 15 intentions need casting when 0 do; the number is noise and he stops reading it.
traces_to: Law 1 (re-deriving the settled is a defect — 60 progressed ideas re-presented as open every session) and Law 7 (a presentation surface collapsed a wrong count into a coherent shape); operator-inbox-is-deterministic-python; ticket 3feb201c84ea (one status, one reader) — this is the same defect one artifact class earlier.
falsifier: From the intent firing, sharpened into teeth: DONE when (1) test_operator_inbox.py's fixture tooth — four ideas on disk, one cited in a fixture ticket's linked_ideas, one named by a fixture intent firing's answers.from_idea, one flagged acted_on, one open — makes read_ideas() count exactly 1 and list only the open one; (2) the intentions fixture tooth — two I-*.md, one cited by a fixture ticket's owning_intention — makes read_intentions() count exactly 1; (3) on the live commons, read_ideas() lists no idea that any intent firing names or any ticket text cites, checked by an INDEPENDENT walk in the proof (a second glob, not the function under test); (4) grep over inbox.py finds no from_idea top-level or provenance-string rule; (5) `cairn operator show inbox` and the codemother dashboard print the same idea count and the same intention count. Horizon: this build session; measured now: 66 ideas listed open, 5 truly open; 15 intentions listed, 0 open under the rule. WRONG INTENT if the idea or intention records are written to (they are Akien's verbatim capture and the intentions' authored text; this is a reader), or if the inventory count is deleted rather than relabeled (Akien 2026-09-07: inventorying all artifacts is a different surface with different display constraints).

questions.a: Three named, each measured. (1) 'A citation anywhere in a ticket means the idea moved on.' Measured 2026-09-07: 53 of 66 ideas are cited by tickets, and the two odd citation shapes (out_of_bounds in e317b0890628, siblings.referent in 8529f0e413b2) are both ALSO in that ticket's linked_ideas, so no false displacement exists today; a future ticket citing an idea only to declare it out of bounds would hide it, and the ticket says so in its falsifier rather than pretending the reader can tell. (2) 'An intent firing's answers.from_idea is the idea's file stem.' Measured: 127 intent firings under ~/.cairn/devices/skill_block/0 (berths/intent, logs/adjudicated/intent, logs/reviewed/intent); from_idea is a str or None; 62 name an idea stem verbatim, the rest read 'none, because ...'. (3) 'The idea record's acted_on is a truthful flag.' Measured: 12 records carry acted_on true; it is written by hand beside acted_on_note, and the reader treats it as one of three voices, never the only one. The load-bearing assumption that stays: the skill_block berth root is where every /intent firing lands (the door writes there and nowhere else, skill_block.py:_write_berth).

Two points were asserted wrapped and were not. (a) The intentions half: 'an intention with a ticket is not an open intention' needs a citation shape, and tickets cite an I-*.md three ways (owning_intention path, a links entry, prose in why). Measured: all 15 I-*.md stems appear in some ticket's serialized text, so the rule is 'stem in ticket text', the same shape as ideas, and the ticket now says so. (b) The dashboard: it prints the counts from the same readers (dashboard.py:95-96), so it needs no second reader, but its INTENTIONS line says 'in intentions-not-beside-code', which is the inventory count the rule replaces with the open count; the wording changes to say what the number now is. Nothing else is asserted wrapped: the inbox's IDEAS section and summary already print from read_ideas, and the operator_inbox_matches_live_state probe reads the same readers, so it moves with them.

Consulted: 7a67ea9907c1 operator-inbox-is-deterministic-python (why: the inbox reads live state and stores nothing) — this cast obeys it, the new reader stores nothing and reads through berth_root(); 3feb201c84ea a-ticket-has-one-status-and-one-reader (why: one reader per derived label) — same shape one artifact class earlier, no collision, the same tool gains one more reader; a705346aa75c operator-show-reaches-all-inbox-items (show_artifact path) — distinct seam, untouched; Law 7 (a presentation surface may collapse an error into a coherent shape, a record of truth never may) — the inbox is a presentation surface and this cast makes it collapse LESS: an idea that moved on is not an error, it is a settled answer being re-presented (Law 1). Distinction recorded, not a collision: 'open in the inbox' (needs his hand) versus 'exists on disk' (inventory). Akien drew it himself 2026-09-07; the ideas and intentions folders remain the inventory and nothing here touches them.

A Haiku-level builder needs: (1) WHERE the intent firings are: every /intent firing is a JSON file under skill_block's berth root and its two log lanes — `berth_root()` from cairn.machines.skill_block.skill_block gives ~/.cairn/devices/skill_block/0/berths; the firings live at <root>/intent/*.json and <root>/../logs/{adjudicated,reviewed}/intent/*.json; the answer is `doc['answers']['from_idea']`, a string that is either an idea file stem or starts with 'none'. Glob `<root.parent>/**/intent/*.json` covers all three lanes. (2) WHAT an idea id is: the idea file's stem, e.g. 2026-09-07-ok-once-an-idea-moves-past-idea; tickets cite it by that stem in linked_ideas or traces_to or intent.from_idea — the reader searches the ticket's serialized JSON text for the stem and stops caring which field. (3) WHAT an intention id is: the I-*.md stem; cited the same way. (4) The three readers are OR'd: an idea has moved on if ANY of intent-firing, ticket-text, acted_on says so. (5) Injectability for the proof: read_ideas(ideas_dir=, tickets_dir=, firings_root=) — the fixture passes temp dirs, exactly the idiom read_lap already uses. (6) The dead code to delete: _acted_on_idea_ids and its from_idea/provenance rule — replace, do not keep beside. (7) The proof idiom: fixture dirs in tempfile, four idea files, one ticket file, one firing file at <firings_root>/berths/intent/x.json — the tooth asserts count == 1 and items[0]['id'] == the open stem. (8) The probe: copy the shape of cairn/tools/system_word/probes/his_case_never_bites.py (survey/trigger/enough/carry, PATIENCE 2, ENOUGH_CLEAN 14); survey() = read_ideas() items older than 14 days by their stem date; it must not subclass BaseDevice. (9) The dashboard wording: dashboard.py:95 prints 'INTENTIONS: n in intentions-not-beside-code' — change to 'INTENTIONS: n open (no ticket yet)' and line 96 to 'IDEAS: n open (not yet at intent)'. Nothing else is left implicit.

constraints: The idea records (CairnCommons/ideas) and the intentions (intentions-not-beside-code) are never written by this reader: they are Akien's verbatim capture and authored text.
One reader for 'has it moved on', in operator_inbox; the dashboard prints from it and globs nothing.
The dead from_idea/provenance rule is deleted, not kept beside the new one.
The inventory count (everything on disk) is a different surface (Akien 2026-09-07) and is not built here; the inbox reports only what needs his hand.
how: One reader in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py decides 'has this idea moved on' three ways in one act: (1) any intent firing (berths/intent + logs/*/intent under skill_block, via berth_root()) whose answers.from_idea names it; (2) any ticket whose serialized text carries its id (linked_ideas, traces_to, intent.from_idea — the field names are what drifted last time, so the reader stops caring which field); (3) the idea record's own acted_on flag. read_intentions returns only I-*.md that no ticket cites. Dashboard and inbox both print from these readers. The proof is a fixture: N ideas, one cited by a ticket in linked_ideas, one named by an intent firing, one flagged acted_on, and the open count is N-3; the intentions tooth likewise. The dead fields (from_idea top-level, provenance string) are deleted, not kept beside the new rule.

watchme.trigger: an idea the inbox lists open whose date (its stem's leading YYYY-MM-DD) is more than fourteen days old, seen on two consecutive surveys — either it is something that genuinely needs his hand and is sitting, or it moved on through a door the three readers cannot see (the recurrence of this very defect); the probe cannot tell which, so it pokes with the three readers' answers for each stale id and lets the owner tell.
watchme.enough: fourteen consecutive clean surveys (no open idea older than fourteen days) after the crossing; the shim counts pulses, not days, the same stated debt every horizon in this corpus carries.
watchme.carrier: a finding against this ticket's falsifier tooth (3): the stale ids, each with its age in days and the three readers' answers (intent firing named it: none; ticket text cites it: none; acted_on: false), so the receiver can tell 'needs his hand' from 'moved on unseen'.
watchme.consumer: codemother, as owner of the care of the code (ruling 2026-09-06), via the harbor master where its watch reads; Akien sees the poke in the inbox's troubles lane.

intent.what: An artifact that has moved to the next stage stops being reported at the earlier one: an idea with an intent firing or a ticket citing it is not an open idea, an intention with a ticket is not an open intention, and the operator inbox lists only what needs Akien's hand.

challenge.back_up: Dashboard prints INTENTIONS: 15 in intentions-not-beside-code; every one of the 15 is cited by a ticket. Under the rule the line reads 0. If Akien wants the inventory count kept somewhere, that is the inventory surface, not the inbox.
challenge.better_approach: Write the displacement at the source instead of deriving it: have /intent's door mark the idea record acted_on when it fires. Rejected as the ONLY mechanism because 53 existing citations live in tickets that will never re-fire, and because the idea record is Akien's verbatim capture — a downstream door writing into it is a second writer on a record with one owner. Deriving from the downstream artifacts costs one glob per read and needs no migration; the door-side mark can be added later as the fast path without changing the answer.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That a ticket citing an idea anywhere means the idea moved on. Measured the two odd citations (out_of_bounds in e317b0890628, siblings.referent in 8529f0e413b2): both ideas are ALSO in that ticket's linked_ideas, so no false displacement today; a future ticket citing an idea only to declare it out of bounds would hide it — the proof does not cover that case and the ticket says so.
challenge.prior_art: 3feb201c84ea (2026-09-06): the same shape — three readers derived a ticket label three ways from fields that had drifted; fixed by one reader. inbox.py's _acted_on_idea_ids already INTENDED this and read from_idea/provenance, fields no ticket ever carried (measured 2026-09-07: 0 of 208 tickets).
challenge.real_collision: None. The inventory question Akien raised is a different surface with different constraints (his words 2026-09-07: 'this is true from a status reporting point of view. if we were inventorying all artifacts that would need different display constraints'); this intent touches status reporting only and leaves the idea and intention records untouched.

why_beneath_the_why: Each stage's door writes its own record and none of them writes back to the record it displaced, so 'is this still open' was never answered anywhere and the inbox answered it by listing everything. The reader derives the displacement from the downstream records; that is the settled answer, computed once (Law 1).
